content:
iPadOS and macOS used to be very different software platforms, but since iPadOS 26, the two have become increasingly similar. This year is even more apparent, as iPadOS 27 adds three features that make the iPad more Mac-like than ever before.

#1: Status bar shows App name

I've been using an M5 iPad Pro with a Magic Keyboard. For keyboard users, the iPad has always had one problem: the lack of a clear "active App" indicator.

If you only have one App on screen, this isn't an issue. But if you can see several Apps at once, using keyboard shortcuts becomes very cumbersome. I can't count how many times I thought a shortcut would trigger within one App, only to find it actually acted on a different App.

Mac solved this problem a long time ago by placing the name of the active App in the upper-left corner of the screen. Now iPadOS 27 does the same thing.

iPadOS 27 users will find the name of the active App right next to other status bar elements (such as time and date). Although it's a small change, it does make using the iPad with a keyboard a much more pleasant experience.

#2: Permanently visible menu bar

Another welcome change in iPadOS 27 is the addition of an option to always show the menu bar.

Last year, Apple brought the menu bar to the iPad for the first time. However, unlike Mac, the menu bar in iPadOS 26 only appeared when the user actively summoned it.

In iPadOS 27, there's a new toggle in the "Multitasking & Gestures" section of the Settings App, called "Automatically show and hide menu bar".

When you turn this toggle off, the menu bar remains visible at all times. I've been using this mode throughout the iPadOS beta period, and it's one of my favourite changes this year.

#3: Mac-like everyday operation speed

Although I love my iPad and appreciate the new features brought by iPadOS 26 and 27, sometimes I get frustrated by how slow some basic operations are. For example, I wrote earlier this year: "Using right-click in iPadOS often feels slow and laggy, but on Mac it's instantly responsive."

Thanks to Apple focusing on fixing bugs this year, I'm happy to say that iPadOS 27 has improved in speed for these kinds of everyday operations.

Apple says context menus brought up by right-clicking with the mouse now open faster, and I can clearly feel it. Browsing files and transferring them to external hard drives is now "up to 5 times faster", and Apple says this speed matches Finder on Mac. App launching is also more responsive, and window management for closing, switching, or dragging windows is faster too.

There are still some areas where Mac is faster and the iPad can feel a bit sluggish. But overall, the speed upgrade in iPadOS 27 is a big step in the right direction.

What are your favourite new features and changes in iPadOS 27? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
